reviews.summary: This proof-of-concept study uses a neural network to predict which radial harmonic dominates a generic-orbit EMRI flux calculation. Frequency-domain Teukolsky computations supply labels for combinations of orbital parameters and mode indices. A nonlinear network substantially outperforms a model linear in the mode numbers: rounded predictions match 88.6% of test labels exactly and 98.5% within one harmonic. The intended benefit is to locate promising modes before spending time on negligible contributions. However, the reported tests split mode samples from the same orbits across training and evaluation, and all backgrounds have spin 0.9. The paper therefore establishes an encouraging mode-selection estimator, rather than a validated general-purpose flux accelerator or a demonstrated waveform-accuracy guarantee.
reviews.relevance_reason: Directly addresses EMRI modeling, Teukolsky fluxes and generic Kerr orbits, with potential computational benefits for perturbative waveform generation.
reviews.quality_reason: A baseline comparison, explicit training setup and quantitative test errors support the restricted proof of concept. Shared orbits across data splits and a single spin weaken evidence of generalization; end-to-end speed and flux-error validation remain necessary.
reviews.limitations: Selective text reading: abstract/introduction, Sec. 2 dataset/truncation excerpts, Sec. 4 network results and Sec. 5 conclusions. No unseen-orbit validation or broad spin coverage; dominant-mode accuracy does not establish total-flux accuracy. No visual figure inspection, training execution or independent derivation verification.
reviews.evidence_location: Sec. 5 Conclusions, discussion of required independent validation.
reviews.evidence_quote: Furthermore the same orbits are included in the training, validation and test datasets.

reviews.summary: This paper separates conditional EMRI phase diagnostics from a proposed spin-matter interpretation. For a prescribed near-zone Kerr deformation, circular-equatorial orbital calculations and a frozen numerical Kerr flux give about −436 radians of conservative dephasing for the chosen benchmark. Comparing another metric with the same leading asymptotic correction produces a much smaller shift, demonstrating dependence on the full metric prescription. Separate spherical Einstein–Cartan appendices report spin-ensemble closure, finite-cloud evolution and coupled metric–matter radiation calculations; these do not derive the rotating ansatz. The useful contribution is an explicit separation of conservative geometry, dissipative assumptions and microphysics. Large phase shifts are not detector forecasts, and a physical source-to-metric map, consistent rotating fluxes and parameter inference are still needed.
reviews.relevance_reason: Directly concerns EMRI dephasing, environmental effects, modified Kerr geometry and coupled matter–metric perturbations.
reviews.quality_reason: The inspected text supplies quantitative vacuum checks, alternative flux/metric comparisons and refinement diagnostics in a separate spherical calculation. These support conditional results, but do not validate the rotating deformation as a sourced model or its observational interpretation.
reviews.limitations: Selective reading: abstract/introduction, Sec. VI interpretation, Sec. VII conclusions, Appendix A checks and portions of Appendix D. The long spin-transport derivations and complete radiation system were not verified. Circular-equatorial rotating results use an assumed flux; spherical radiation results concern a different model. No visual figure inspection or code execution.
reviews.evidence_location: Sec. VII Conclusions and Discussion, interpretation of the rotating phase diagnostic.
reviews.evidence_quote: The calculation therefore supports neither detectability nor dark-matter or fundamental-coupling bounds.

reviews.summary: The study asks whether gravitational radiation from an accretion flow records the disk’s tilt relative to a spinning black hole. Two matched three-dimensional GRMHD simulations, initially aligned or tilted by 75 degrees, supply stress–energy sources for time-domain Teukolsky calculations on a fixed Kerr background. The tilted flow contributes more power to higher azimuthal modes; as it aligns, the high-mode fraction declines alongside the measured tilt. Mode-cutoff checks and MRI resolution diagnostics support the numerical example, while a rotated-axis model provides a geometric interpretation. This connects disk dynamics to a potentially useful multimode gravitational-wave signature. Generality and observability remain open: only two initial orientations and one spin are studied, and the illustrative strain rescaling is not a detector-inference analysis.
reviews.relevance_reason: Combines GRMHD, Teukolsky radiation, environmental geometry and gravitational waves, directly matching several central topics.
reviews.quality_reason: Matched simulations, mode-cutoff comparisons and MRI diagnostics substantiate the reported correlation. A narrow simulation set and idealized strain rescaling limit claims of universal tilt recovery or detectability.
reviews.limitations: Selective text reading: abstract/introduction, Sec. II setup and observables, Sec. III result excerpts, Secs. IV–VI and Appendices A–B. Fixed background, single spin and two initial tilts; disk self-gravity and detector parameter recovery are not assessed here. Mode-cutoff agreement is not a full numerical-resolution study. No visual figure inspection, simulation execution or derivation verification.
reviews.evidence_location: Sec. III, discussion of Figure 3(d), convergence with azimuthal mode cutoff.
reviews.evidence_quote: The ratios obtained with m_{\max}=5 , 6, and 7 closely agree

reviews.summary: This spectral survey follows charged-black-hole gravitational quasinormal modes through crossings of the negative imaginary frequency axis. Analytic continuation of the ingoing horizon solution identifies zeros of the incoming amplitude at infinity, with a separate construction at exact extremality. For angular orders two and three, the authors trace 42 overtone families each: 75 retain finite damping at extremality, while nine approach zero frequency with vanishing excitation. The analysis also distinguishes algebraically special quasinormal and total-transmission solutions, and identifies strong excitation-factor resonances between selected overtones. Detailed residual and parameter-refinement checks support this bounded survey. It supplies useful mode identities and continuation seeds, but neither proves completeness for all angular orders and overtones nor establishes source-dependent ringdown amplitudes.
reviews.relevance_reason: Directly addresses black-hole perturbations, quasinormal modes, extremal limits and resonant excitation, central to the selected topics.
reviews.quality_reason: Explicit boundary/sheet conventions, independent exact-extremal constructions, amplitude residuals and precision/radial-setting checks give substantial support within the surveyed mode range. The inspected validation concerns numerical consistency rather than independent reproduction.
reviews.limitations: Selective reading: abstract/introduction, Sec. II opening, Sec. III.3 transport, Sec. IV.3 extremal checks, excitation-factor caveat and Sec. V conclusions. Only the gravitational branch at angular orders 2 and 3 and 42 families each is surveyed. Source integrals and waveform interference are not calculated. No visual figure inspection, code execution or independent derivation verification.
reviews.evidence_location: End of Sec. IV.2, interpretation of excitation factors.
reviews.evidence_quote: Their contributions to a waveform also depend on the source integrals and on interference between modes.

reviews.summary: The abstract describes a framework for gravitational-wave backgrounds generated by slowly evolving early-Universe sources. Starting from a constant-in-time source model, the authors incorporate decay through a coherent unequal-time correlator and discuss applications to MHD turbulence, sound waves and bubble collisions. They report that long source-decorrelation times support the constant-in-time or coherent-decay description, whereas short decorrelation can add a resonant contribution. The proposed spectrum rises cubically in the infrared, has an intermediate linear regime and acquires a source-dependent ultraviolet slope. The framework aims to explain differing radiation efficiencies of sound waves and turbulence and unify several source classes. These are abstract-level claims here: the derivations, numerical comparisons and range of applicability were unavailable within the review’s text-size limit.
reviews.relevance_reason: Relevant to gravitational-wave backgrounds, turbulence and resonance, but focused on cosmological sources rather than EMRIs or astrophysical black-hole perturbations.
reviews.quality_reason: Only the abstract is available in the prepared packet because the full text exceeds the review limit. The derivations and validation cannot be assessed from this evidence.
reviews.limitations: Abstract only. No full-paper sections, equations, figures or numerical validation inspected; claims of agreement and spectral universality are reported from the abstract, not independently evaluated.

reviews.summary: This paper interprets black-hole ringdown excitation as spectral filtering of the perturbation. Factoring each excitation coefficient into a background response and a source overlap shows that the relevant spectrum is weighted by the quasinormal-mode wavefunction; it reduces to an ordinary Fourier transform for distant initial data. Tunable Gaussian pulses vary bandwidth and carrier frequency, allowing selective mode excitation. Regge–Wheeler evolutions, full radial-wavefunction calculations and asymptotic predictions agree closely in the tested regime, while sliding-window fits expose tail contamination and fitting ambiguity. The contribution is a quantitative, controllable interpretation of source-dependent ringdown amplitudes. Applications to rotating holes and nonlinear merger waveforms remain extensions, and window-to-window spread should not be read as a calibrated statistical posterior.
reviews.relevance_reason: Direct overlap with quasinormal modes, resonances, black-hole perturbation theory and gravitational-wave ringdown excitation.
reviews.quality_reason: Analytic factorization, two radial descriptions and direct time-domain comparisons provide complementary support for the tested pulse families. The paper explicitly identifies tail-driven fit floors and finite-source-location limitations.
reviews.limitations: Selective reading: abstract/introduction, asymptotic-validity excerpts, Sec. VI.4 numerical validation and most of Sec. VIII discussion. Demonstrations concern linear Regge–Wheeler evolutions and controlled initial pulses, not observed mergers or Kerr waveform inference. Fit-window dispersion is an empirical systematic diagnostic. No visual figure inspection, code execution or independent derivation verification.
reviews.evidence_location: Sec. VIII Discussion and Conclusion, distinction between weighted overlap and asymptotic Fourier transform.
reviews.evidence_quote: The standard Fourier transform arises in the asymptotic limit.

reviews.summary: Ultralight-dark-matter interference granules can act as a random diffractive screen for strongly lensed gravitational waves. The authors construct projected density realizations from a Gaussian field covariance and compute their full wave-optics response around minimum and saddle macroimages. Modulations become strongest when the Fresnel scale approaches the granule coherence length, reaching percent levels in benchmark halos and larger values near critical curves. LISA massive-black-hole-binary examples suggest distinguishability near boson masses of 10⁻²¹ eV. A Fourier implementation is checked against contour integration for minimum images. The contribution is a statistical granular-lensing model beyond leading Born order. However, fixed intrinsic source parameters make the detectability estimates optimistic; realistic halo correlations, smooth-lens degeneracies and full inference are still required.
reviews.relevance_reason: Directly studies gravitational-wave lensing and environmental dark-matter structure, with wave-optics calculations relevant to the lensing topic.
reviews.quality_reason: The projected stochastic model, nonperturbative phase-screen calculation, ensembles and cross-code comparison provide substantial support for benchmark modulation predictions. The paper clearly limits its mismatch-based detectability criterion and near-critical host approximation.
reviews.limitations: Selective reading: abstract/introduction, Sec. V.1 detection setup, most of Sec. VI conclusions and Appendix B convergence/GLoW comparison. Local host expansion is least reliable near critical curves; no soliton or self-gravity correlations. Intrinsic source parameters are fixed, and comparison-code checks cover Type I images. No visual figure inspection, code execution or independent derivation verification.
reviews.evidence_location: Sec. V.1 Setup, limitation of the waveform mismatch calculation.
reviews.evidence_quote: We hold the intrinsic source parameters fixed when comparing the lensed signal with the reference template.

reviews.summary: The authors calculate gravitational-wave production from a cosmological magnetic field concentrated in a narrow band of wavenumbers. Approximating that band by a delta function makes the anisotropic-stress convolution analytic, producing a spectrum with a peak and sharp cutoff at twice the magnetic wavenumber. Applied to an ultralight-axion magnetogenesis scenario near recombination, the attainable signal is too weak to explain pulsar-timing backgrounds at allowed magnetic energy densities. Scaling the calculation to earlier generation epochs gives a conditional estimate near 160 MeV and a rough lower temperature range of 1–10 MeV for viable explanations. This provides a useful analytic mapping from magnetic structure to gravitational radiation, but broader spectra, evolving turbulence and data-level likelihood comparisons can change its quantitative interpretation.
reviews.relevance_reason: Relevant to stochastic gravitational waves, magnetic turbulence and resonance-driven production, with a cosmological focus peripheral to the main EMRI and black-hole topics.
reviews.quality_reason: An explicit narrow-band construction, source-timescale argument and reported numerical check support the analytic estimates. Temperature bounds rely on spectral, energy-density and source-evolution assumptions rather than a full PTA inference.
reviews.limitations: Selective reading: abstract/introduction, Sec. III narrow-band/time-independence argument, Sec. IV temperature-bound excerpts and Sec. V conclusion. The delta-spectrum approximation is less secure near the horizon scale at the quoted QCD epoch. Turbulent decay and broad-spectrum histories are simplified. No visual figure inspection, numerical reproduction or independent derivation verification.
reviews.evidence_location: Sec. III, immediately before the delta-function magnetic spectrum in Eq. (30).
reviews.evidence_quote: we approximate P_{B}(k) as highly-peaked at the critical wavenumber k_{c}

reviews.summary: This work derives a geometric sufficient condition for convergence of Kerr quasinormal-mode overtone sums at fixed angular indices. High-damping asymptotics relate the growth of Green-function pole amplitudes to optical distances from source and observer to characteristic bounce radii. Different angular behavior of prolate and oblate mode families introduces directional dependence and bounce surfaces. Numerical amplitudes at spin 0.7 reproduce the predicted spatial growth rates to better than one percent on the tested grid. The contribution is a concrete boundary for absolute convergence of these pole sums, relevant to interpreting early ringdown fits. It is not a complete representation of the causal response: nonpole contributions remain necessary, and an extended physical source requires integration over its emitting history and position.
reviews.relevance_reason: Directly concerns Kerr perturbations, quasinormal-mode expansions and the validity of gravitational-wave ringdown models, central to black-hole perturbation theory.
reviews.quality_reason: The asymptotic growth criterion, angular/radial decomposition, Schwarzschild limit and direct checks of complete pole amplitudes provide complementary support. The inspected numerical comparison is bounded in spin and sampled positions; full-source implications remain to be developed.
reviews.limitations: Selective text reading: abstract/introduction, Sec. II.1 convergence bound, Sec. VI conclusions and Appendix D.2–D.3 amplitude checks. Fixed-multipole pole sums exclude the rest of the Green-function integral. A sufficient convergence threshold does not establish first signal arrival or a reliable nonlinear ringdown-fit start time. No visual figure inspection, code execution or independent derivation verification.
reviews.evidence_location: Sec. VI Conclusions, distinction between convergence and causal arrival.
reviews.evidence_quote: the QNM sums can converge before any signal reaches the observer.

reviews.summary: The abstract presents a scalar-wave framework for corrections to Newtonian point-mass gravitational-wave lensing. Newtonian-dressed radial kernels retain the long-range interaction while organizing additional effects by distance from the lens. The authors report that wavefront curvature modifies the direct wave as well as the scattered component, and that steeper exterior potentials require local terms fixed by the lens’s inner boundary condition. Matching to a Schwarzschild horizon supplies an absorptive contribution that reproduces the horizon-area cross section and can cancel finite-distance corrections for aligned sources. The contribution is a systematic connection between exterior lens structure and central absorption beyond the thin-lens description. Only the abstract was available here, so the matching calculation, error control and applicability to tensor gravitational waves remain unassessed.
reviews.relevance_reason: Directly addresses wave-optics gravitational lensing, black-hole boundary conditions and perturbative wave propagation, closely aligned with the lensing and perturbation topics.
reviews.quality_reason: The prepared source is abstract-only because the full text exceeds the review limit. Technical matching, regularization and claimed cross-section agreement cannot be evaluated from the abstract.
reviews.limitations: Abstract only. No derivations, full-paper sections, figures or numerical checks inspected. The described calculation uses a scalar wave; implications for tensor gravitational waves require examining the full treatment.
